title: Decide whether letting go of a drag should land a measurement
goal: There are two ways to draw a distance measurement in the app: three clicks, which is what everyone gets, and one drag that lands the moment you let go, which is switched off. A walk in the repo tests the drag one and reports success while nothing at all was measured, so nobody can tell which of the two the product means. Pick one and make the walk say the truth.
notes: Reproduced 2026-09-08. Ran Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/distance-lands-on-release.json against the probe build. Log at /tmp/photonz-playtest/distance-lands-on-release/log.json: step 8 drags (234,786)->(480,786) in distance mode and step 10 (stage 1-button-width, note "one drag, number placed by the app") reports measures=[]. The caliper is sitting in .secondPlaced waiting for a third click. Two separate causes: (a) Experiments measureDistanceLandsOnRelease is a sub-flag of next-measure-modes and is off, so CanvasMeasure.measureLandsOnRelease is false and advanceMeasurePlacement goes to .secondPlaced instead of committing; (b) the walk re-arms with a bare key i at step 11, which cycles the MODE rather than the tool, so stage 2 is actually measured in Size mode, not Distance, and that is the only reason the walk ends with any measurements at all. Use the measureMode step to arm a mode. The new measuring field in a walk log now names the in-flight state, which is how this was spotted.
acceptance: It is written down which way a distance measurement is meant to be drawn, and the app ships that way
Scripts/playtest/distance-lands-on-release.json either proves what it claims or is replaced by one that does
No walk in Scripts/playtest reports a measurement in a stage where its own log shows none
